title: Shopify AI assistant for stock and fulfilment reviews
h1: a shopify assistant for store exceptions worth checking
description: Review Shopify stock, draft orders and fulfilment work with Dusk Bot. See the custom sign-in requirement and routines that leave store records unchanged.
answer: a shopify bot can inspect orders, stock by location and draft orders to prepare a store operations review. dusk bot can schedule those checks, but this toolkit needs your own composio project key and auth configuration because managed sign-in is not available. start with the listed read actions and keep stock changes, refunds and customer messages outside the review.
og_line: review stock before changing the store.

app.name: Shopify
app.intro: store work benefits from a narrow exception list. ask which draft orders need a decision or which locations have low stock, with the source records beside each point. use these specific reads first rather than assuming every broad graphql action is allowed for a read-only bot.

highlight.use: identify the store locations before comparing their stock
check inventory levels at the location you specify
inspect a known order when reviewing a fulfilment question
read product details for a catalog correction list
review drafts that still need a store owner's decision
list assigned fulfilment work for an operations check
inspect returned abandoned checkouts without sending recovery messages
prepare an agreed draft order when you explicitly allow changes

app.setup: this shopify toolkit has no ready-made composio sign-in as of 12 november 2026. add your own composio project key and auth config under **Settings**, **API keys**; on dusk cloud, ask support first. once connected, identify the store and locations. allow only the bot that needs store access.

routines_intro: these messages request operations notes, not automatic store maintenance. set the stock threshold, location and age rules yourself so the bot is checking your policy rather than inventing one.

routines.name: location stock exceptions
routines.message: every weekday at 7, check inventory levels for the shopify location i named. list items below the minimums i supplied, with the returned quantity and location. do not adjust stock or assume incoming deliveries. flag missing inventory data separately.

routines.name: draft orders needing a decision
routines.message: every tuesday at 1, list our shopify draft orders and apply the age rule i gave you. bring me drafts that need a decision, with their recorded details. do not complete drafts, send invoices or contact customers.

routines.name: fulfilment desk check
routines.message: every afternoon at 4, list the assigned shopify fulfilment orders available to this connection. highlight the ones matching our supplied exception rules and inspect known order details when needed. leave holds, routing and fulfilment status unchanged.
routines.output: an operations note for the fulfilment desk

asks:
the reviews above need no store writes. read-only access prevents draft creation, inventory adjustments and order edits, even when a suggested correction sounds straightforward. grant a specific write action only when that is part of the job you intended.

customer messages and other sends ask first by default, unless you choose a daily sending allowance. one exception: a bot on **Full access** with no sending rule of its own may send up to 25 a day without asking, so give full-access bots **Ask every time** under sending. inventory changes and order maintenance are not documented as having that same approval step. if you allow those actions, tell the bot "ask me before you change anything" and keep its permitted action list small.
cannot: connect using a composio-managed shopify sign-in in the current catalog. custom auth setup must work before these routines can inspect your store.
call every graphql lookup with read-only access. the broad shopify graphql orders, products and inventory actions are classified as changes here; use the highlighted read actions for these routines.
correct stock or complete draft orders when you have allowed only reads. a stock warning is a prompt to investigate, not a stock adjustment.
run an early stock check on a computer that is asleep. local routines stop while dusk bot is closed or the computer sleeps; dusk cloud can host them on an awake machine.

sections.h: let the store owner define an exception
sections.md:
give the bot a minimum stock level for each relevant item and the location it belongs to. tell it whether a blank value is missing data or a value your process treats specially. a low number alone does not establish that you should reorder.

for a broader working day, see [bots for ecommerce](/for/ecommerce). keep any [payment review](/integrations/stripe) tied to its own connected account rather than assuming a store order proves money arrived.

sections.h: keep customer follow-ups as a separate job
sections.md: an abandoned checkout list is a review input, not permission to contact people. if customer support also uses [whatsapp business](/integrations/whatsapp), connect that app separately and define which facts may go into a reply. review the recipient and promise before any send.

faq.q: can claude help manage my shopify store?
faq.a: a bot in dusk bot can use the catalog actions once the custom connection is configured. begin with a precise read-only job such as checking stock at one location, then decide whether it should gain any write actions.

faq.q: why is this not a one-click shopify connection?
faq.a: composio, the connection service, has no ready-made shopify sign-in. it needs your own composio project key and auth config. the catalog listing alone does not mean a managed connection is ready.

faq.q: will it automatically change stock when it finds a problem?
faq.a: not with read-only access. the stock routine only reports exceptions. if you later permit stock changes, explicitly require the bot to ask before changing anything rather than assuming a send approval covers inventory edits.
